title: Peleș Castle

visualBrief: Complete principal Peleș Castle exterior, including both mapped parents, all connected main and returned ranges around the actual western courtyard, the square clock tower with open gallery arches and closed clock panels, its steep roof and open lantern/spire, the polygonal half-timber front tower, two separate white turrets, slate gables and hips, closed dormers, chimneys, a closed central glass roof with fitted curb, the front veranda, through-gateway and low eastern retaining gallery. Original simplified timber and stone trim; figurative murals, sculpture, inscriptions, heraldry and interiors are excluded. Independent estate buildings, gardens and forest remain native context.

Three ordinary front, court-corner and oblique aerial pictures were inspected. Rear and roof inventories, concealed joins, original clock and gable trim, window rhythm, timber patterns, terrace shapes and historic grades are medium-fi approximations. Lower garden works and independent estate structures are outside the principal-building scope. Context is synthetic; physical device timings and numerical LOD errors remain unmeasured.

Seven existing shared 256px plaster, limestone, granite, wood, slate, copper and window-grid graphs; metric UVs, linear colors and no private or embedded images. Four separately authored browser tiers retain the complete mapped composition. Skyline simplifies small contours, lantern posts and approaches; district uses window proxies and timber bands; street uses closed recesses; close-up adds timber braces and roof trim; the detailed master preserves finer framing.

references.observed: Southwest/front panorama: pale lower stone and plaster, dark red-brown half-timber upper ranges, steep gray slate roofs, a tall square clock tower with open upper gallery, clock panels and lantern/spire, a projecting polygonal timber tower and separate white round turrets. Trees conceal parts of the lower frontage.

Inner-court corner: pale lower walls with closed doors and greenish glazing; timber upper galleries and white infill; stone arches and stairs. This picture does not establish the whole courtyard plan. Figurative murals, sculpture, lettering and fountain figures are excluded; trim is original and simplified.

Oblique aerial: complete irregular principal palace with both returns, separate tower groups, steep slate gables and hips, many chimneys and red-brown lower veranda roofs. The large central glazed unit is closed and distinct from the actual western court. Garden works and forest are surrounding context.

Union of main way 1454368027 clips 9/88/89/144/167 and attached front way 1454368026 clips 8/87/143/166. Both parents are necessary for the clock/front-tower group. 148 parent and 3D components have at least 98% coverage; all 31 independent estate/context components remain native.
